{"items": ["[passage_read_so_far]
- Lanyon receives a registered letter from Henry Jekyll on the ninth of January.（Dr. Lanyon、Dr. Jekyll）
- Jekyll begs Lanyon to help him, saying his life and reason are at stake.（Dr. Jekyll、Dr. Lanyon）
- Jekyll orders Poole to wait with a locksmith for Lanyon's arrival.（Dr. Jekyll、Poole）
- Jekyll instructs Lanyon to force open his cabinet and take the fourth drawer.（Dr. Jekyll、Dr. Lanyon）
- Jekyll asks Lanyon to receive a midnight messenger and hand over the drawer.（Dr. Jekyll、Dr. Lanyon）
- Jekyll warns that if the night passes without event, Lanyon has seen the last of him.（Dr. Jekyll）
- Lanyon suspects Jekyll is insane but feels bound to obey the appeal.（Dr. Lanyon、Dr. Jekyll）
- Lanyon drives to Jekyll's house, where the butler awaits him.（Dr. Lanyon、Poole）
- The carpenter and locksmith work two hours to open Jekyll's cabinet door.（Dr. Lanyon、the carpenter、the locksmith）
- Lanyon takes the drawer, has it packed in straw and a sheet, and returns home.（Dr. Lanyon）
- Lanyon examines the drawer's powders, phial, and book of dated experiments.（Dr. Lanyon）
- Lanyon dismisses his servants and loads an old revolver for self-defence.（Dr. Lanyon）
- At midnight a small man knocks gently and crouches against the portico pillars.（Dr. Lanyon、the small man）
- Lanyon asks if the visitor comes from Dr. Jekyll, and the man gestures yes.（Dr. Lanyon、the small man）
- The visitor glances back at a policeman and hurries inside.（the small man、the policeman）
- Lanyon sees the visitor clearly for the first time and is struck by his appearance.（Dr. Lanyon、the small man）
- Hyde enters Lanyon's house and urgently asks if he has it（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Lanyon rebukes Hyde for forgetting they are unacquainted（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Hyde says he comes at the instance of Dr. Henry Jekyll（the man in the middle、Dr. Jekyll）
- Lanyon points Hyde to the drawer holding the package（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Hyde uncovers the contents and sobs with immense relief（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Hyde mixes the red tincture and powder into a changing compound（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Hyde offers Lanyon knowledge and power or to leave unwiser（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Lanyon agrees to see the end of the inexplicable service（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Hyde drinks the glass at one gulp and cries out（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle）
- Hyde transforms and Henry Jekyll stands before Lanyon（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle、Dr. Jekyll）
- Jekyll confesses his moral turpitude to Lanyon with tears（Dr. Lanyon、Dr. Jekyll）
- Lanyon learns the visitor was Hyde, murderer of Carew（Dr. Lanyon、the man in the middle、Sir Danvers Carew）

Dr. Lanyon receives a desperate letter from Henry Jekyll, who begs him to break into his cabinet, take the fourth drawer, and hand it to a midnight messenger. Lanyon obeys, waits armed, and admits a small, crouching man who claims to come from Jekyll. The visitor mixes and drinks the drawer's chemicals, then transforms before Lanyon's eyes into Henry Jekyll, who tearfully confesses that the messenger was Hyde, murderer of Sir Danvers Carew."], "dimensions": {"d0": {"labels": ["supported", "beyond_text", "contradicted"], "instructions": "A spoiler-free reading companion wrote the note below about a novel.
